name: Zentauri UI
claim: React + Tailwind v4, token-first, axe-core in CI
body: A component library published to npm as @zentauri-ui/zentauri-components. The interesting parts are the API surface — how much a consumer has to know to use a component correctly — and keeping motion optional without leaking implementation detail into props. Accessibility is exercised in CI rather than documented: 46 dedicated tests pair axe-core audits with keyboard interaction across every interactive and compound component, each asserting zero violations.

name: Playwright automation suite
claim: E2E, API, snapshot, a11y, link validation, auth flows
body: A test suite that covers end-to-end flows, API contracts, UI snapshots, accessibility checks, link validation, and authentication workflows. The goal was release confidence: making a green pipeline mean something specific rather than something vague.

name: Multi-brand monorepo CMS
body: A CMS serving several brands from one monorepo. Shared primitives and per-brand overrides, so adding a brand is configuration rather than a fork. The measurable outcome was onboarding speed for a new brand and how much code stayed shared.

name: Orbit
claim: WebGL n-body simulation with live telemetry
body: A gravitational simulation built for this site: four masses attracting each other pairwise, and two thousand massless test particles integrated against them with semi-implicit Euler and softened gravity. It reports its own frame time, particle count and device pixel ratio, halves its workload when it falls behind, stops entirely when off-screen or hidden, and never downloads at all below 1024px. It runs in WebGL not because two thousand particles demand a GPU, but because this site already loads three.js for its backdrop — so the simulation costs a few kilobytes of code instead of a second renderer.
